# function: parse_passwd_line

Parses one line of `/etc/passwd` (`name:password:uid:gid:gecos:home:shell`, see `passwd(5)`) and returns an object with the attributes `name`, `password` (usually `x`, as the hash is in `/etc/shadow`), `uid`, `gid`, `gecos`, `home` and `shell`.

Returns `null` for a blank line or a `#` comment, so that a whole file can be parsed with a `for` expression that skips them. A line with other than seven fields, an empty name or a `uid` or `gid` that is not a number between 0 and 4294967295 is an error, and so is an argument with more than one line. To look up a user of the host the provider runs on, use the `sysutils_user` data source instead.

Provider-defined functions need Terraform 1.8 or later, or OpenTofu 1.7 or later, and a `required_providers` entry for `blechschmidt/sysutils`; call it as `provider::sysutils::parse_passwd_line(...)`. It is pure: it only parses its argument, never reads files or looks at the host, so its result is the same during plan and apply. Use `file()` or the [`sysutils_file`](../data-sources/file.md) data source to read the input.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "sysutils_file" "passwd" {
  path = "/etc/passwd"
}

locals {
  # Blank lines and comments parse to null and are skipped.
  accounts = [
    for line in split("\n", data.sysutils_file.passwd.content) :
    provider::sysutils::parse_passwd_line(line)
    if provider::sysutils::parse_passwd_line(line) != null
  ]
}

output "login_users" {
  value = sort([
    for a in local.accounts : a.name
    if a.uid >= 1000 && !endswith(a.shell, "nologin") && !endswith(a.shell, "false")
  ])
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
parse_passwd_line(line string) object
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `line` (String) One line of a passwd file. A trailing `\n` or `\r\n` is ignored.
